The factorial upper bound proves all Schatten classes and injection. Tail hazard monotonicity proves a strict ordered no-skipping modal staircase. Uniform Poisson geometric-tail expansion and Stirling, with Chernoff suppression outside the unique saddle v=u, give the exact exponential rate and inverse-square-root prefactor; the floor(ux) lower test matches the upper bound. The finite checker passed 674 assertions; no finite experiment is treated as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Semantic searches of published mathematical findings, published relevant finding full texts, and three principal published-paper full-text checks were compared by operator, spectrum, and implication. The closest general cross-Toeplitz calculus does not state disk transfer singular values or the fixed-weight-mismatch sharp saddle-point norm. The 2026 Fock Toeplitz disk bound covers the equal-weight endpoint but not the growing compactly supported exponential symbol. Prior full-space Gaussian projections have geometric spectra, and Landau interlevel disk transfer has Poisson-mass rather than Poisson-tail coefficients. The exact distinct claim is the cross-weight disk staircase and exponential norm law with its 1/sqrt(radius-squared) constant. A risk of an earlier equivalent radial-Toeplitz asymptotic remains.
residual_risks: An older radial Toeplitz treatment of the compactly supported exponential symbol may contain the same saddle-point norm formula under different notation.
Full text of Fang--Tien arXiv:2610.41461 was not obtained; only the abstract was available.

value.rationale: A compact observation window between differently weighted analytic Hilbert spaces regularizes an otherwise unbounded comparison of Fock norms. The exact amplification exponent and especially its nontrivial x^{-1/2} prefactor quantify how costly that regularization becomes with observation radius. The exact monotone modal staircase and exponentially small first mismatch threshold identify the concentration-mode instability rather than merely restating standard diagonalization. This is a motivated sharp norm problem for natural Fock transfers, not an arbitrary parameter slice; no general paper-sized consequence is asserted.
